text: What are flowcharts used for in troubleshooting?

options.text: Recording faults in a database for future reference
Visual yes/no decision diagrams that guide you to a fault
Software tools that test hardware components automatically
Step-by-step written instructions for solving known problems

explanation: Flowcharts are visual yes/no decision diagrams that guide a technician to a fault. They are great for common, repeatable problems.

options.text: For complex, unique faults never seen before
For common, repeatable problems
Only when other tools have failed
For testing hardware at a code level

explanation: Flowcharts are great for common, repeatable problems where the decision tree can be mapped out in advance.

text: What is a helpdesk used for in troubleshooting?

options.text: Automatically diagnosing hardware faults
A support team or service to contact when stuck — often the first point of contact for users reporting problems
A searchable database of past faults and solutions
Official manuals for hardware and software

explanation: A helpdesk is a support team or service to contact when stuck. It is often the first point of contact for users reporting problems.

text: What are diagnostic and debugging tools used for?

options.text: Providing yes/no decision trees for common faults
Software tools that test hardware or code to identify exactly where a fault lies
Storing records of previous faults and how they were fixed
Official product support from the manufacturer

explanation: Diagnostic and debugging tools are software tools that test hardware or code to identify exactly where a fault lies. They are especially useful for larger programmes.

options.text: Visual flowcharts showing yes/no decisions
Step-by-step written instructions for solving known problems
Software that automatically repairs faults
Databases of manufacturer warranty information

explanation: Troubleshooting guides are step-by-step written instructions for solving known problems. They are quick to follow and good for common faults.

text: What is a knowledge base in the context of troubleshooting?

options.text: A visual diagram showing how components connect
A searchable database of known faults and solutions built up over time
The operating manual supplied with a device
A live chat service provided by the manufacturer

explanation: A knowledge base is a searchable database of known faults and solutions built up over time — either by colleagues with specialist knowledge or through accumulated experience.

text: What are handbooks used for in troubleshooting?

options.text: Logging faults as they are discovered
Official manuals for hardware or software containing technical specs and fault-finding procedures
Providing remote access to fix faults
Visual decision trees for common faults

explanation: Handbooks are official manuals for hardware or software containing technical specifications and fault-finding procedures.

text: What is the value of internet resources when troubleshooting?

options.text: They provide legally binding repair instructions
Forums, articles and community sites where others may have already solved the same problem
They automatically diagnose the fault remotely
They replace the need for manufacturer support

explanation: Internet resources such as forums, articles and community sites are valuable because others may have already encountered and solved the same problem.

text: Why are manufacturer websites and support considered one of the most reliable sources?

options.text: They are free to access and always available
They provide official support direct from the maker of the hardware or software
They contain community-contributed solutions from experienced users
They automatically update your device firmware

explanation: Manufacturer websites and support are often the most reliable source for specific product issues because they come directly from the people who made the hardware or software.

text: What are fault log databases used for?

options.text: Diagnosing hardware faults automatically
Records of previous faults and how they were fixed — invaluable for spotting patterns or recurring issues
Providing step-by-step guides for common problems
Connecting to manufacturer support services

explanation: Fault log databases are records of previous faults and how they were fixed. They are invaluable for spotting patterns or recurring issues and for speeding up future repairs.

text: How many diagnostic tools and methods are covered in this module?
explanation: There are 9 tools: Flowcharts, Helpdesks, Diagnostics & Debugging Tools, Troubleshooting Guides, Experts & Knowledge Bases, Handbooks, Internet Resources, Manufacturer Websites & Support, and Fault Log Databases.

text: What factor should influence which diagnostic tool or resource you use?

options.text: Always use the internet first as it is the fastest
The type of problem and your company's policies
Always contact the manufacturer regardless of the fault
Use fault logs only — they contain all known solutions

explanation: The right tool depends on the type of problem and your company's policies. No single tool is always best — different situations call for different resources.

text: Match each diagnostic tool to its correct description.

columnB.text: Official manual with technical specs and fault-finding procedures
Visual yes/no decision diagram guiding you to a fault
Records of past faults and fixes, useful for spotting recurring issues
Support team — often the first point of contact for users reporting problems

explanation: Flowchart = visual yes/no diagram. Fault Log Database = records of past faults. Handbook = official manual. Helpdesk = first point of contact support.
